# Iddhipāda Saṁyutta (SN 51)

**ID:** SN 51
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Iddhipāda Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul6.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Iddhipāda Saṁyutta* (SN 51) is the fifty-first collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated within the *Mahāvagga* (Great Chapter) among the core collections dealing with the thirty-seven qualities that contribute to awakening (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*) [Gethin 2008]. The saṁyutta contains 86 discourses addressing the four bases of spiritual power or accomplishment (*iddhipāda*): desire or enthusiasm (*chanda*), energy (*viriya*), consciousness or mind (*citta*), and investigation (*vīmaṁsā*), each developed together with concentration (*samādhi*) and formative striving (*padhāna-saṅkhāra*) [Bodhi 2003; Gethin 2001; Hazra 1994]. While the higher purpose of the Buddhist path is liberation and arahantship, the discourses explain that developing meditative immersion through these four bases can yield both supernormal powers (*iddhi*) and supreme knowledge; past, present, and future ascetics and brahmins, including the Buddha himself, achieve spiritual mastery through them [Bodhi 2003].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- This file contains 3 suttas; 3 of them have known parallels. Full parallels by collection: Pali (1), SĀ (1)
- Examples of full non-Pali parallels: SN 51.15 Uṇṇābhabrāhmaṇasutta ↔ SA 561 婆羅門

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Saṁyutta Nikāya (2000/2003) — Explained the meaning of iddhipāda, its role in achieving supernormal powers and arahantship, and universal claims about ascetics and the Buddha.
- [Gethin 2001] R. M. L. Gethin, The Buddhist Path to Awakening: A Study of the Bodhi-Pakkhiya Dhammā (2001 [1992]) — Discussed the formulaic components of the iddhipādas, textual analysis in the samyutta, and prolongation of life.
- [Gethin 2008] Rupert Gethin, Sayings of the Buddha: New Translations from the Pali Nikāyas (2008) — Identified the position of the Iddhipāda Saṁyutta within the Mahāvagga and among the seven sets of bodhipakkhiyā dhammā.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Enumerated the four components of the iddhis in SN 51.
- [Nyanatiloka 1957] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Piṭaka (1957) — Identified the correspondence between SN 51.13 and the Suttanta-bhājanīya of the Abhidhamma Vibhaṅga.
